summary: Ustaz Azlan corrects several slips from the previous episode, then tells the story behind Surah Al-Kawthar when Abu Lahab rejoiced at the death of the Prophet's SAW son. He explains Quraysh's character-assassination campaign: calling the Prophet SAW mad, a sorcerer, a poet and a liar, and creating inferiority among poor followers by mocking them. Stories include Umar hearing Surah Al-Haqqah first-hand, and Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah's admission of the Quran's beauty answered by Al-Muddaththir verses 11-26. He closes with a preview of the phase of physical intimidation and the family of Yasir.
keyPoints: Surah Al-Kawthar came down to console the Prophet SAW when Abu Lahab greeted the death of his son with 'cut off'.
After failing to stop the Quran, Quraysh turned to character assassination though they knew he was the most honest.
The labels used were mad, sorcerer, poet, soothsayer and liar; Quranic verses exposed each of them.
Quraysh created inferiority among the followers by mocking the poor and different.
Umar heard the Prophet SAW recite Al-Haqqah behind the Kaaba's covering and felt Islam enter his heart, though the chain is weak.
Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah admitted the Quran's beauty but chose to reject it out of interest, so Allah exposed his plotting.
The best defence is to explain what the Quran is, not merely deny the accusations.

lessons.title: Correct mistakes honestly
lessons.body: The ustaz corrects slips, especially those touching the names of companions.

lessons.title: The Prophet's SAW name is not cut off
lessons.body: Muhammad is the most given name in the world; it is his haters who are cut off.

lessons.title: The Prophet's SAW character cannot be killed
lessons.body: No one who lived with him found a flaw.

lessons.title: Beware labels as a tactic
lessons.body: The more labels thrown, the more people fear without hearing the real message.

lessons.title: Reformers are often labelled
lessons.body: Those who bring change are often called agents or mad.

lessons.title: The best defence is explaining what the Quran is
lessons.body: The Quran answers accusations by stating what it is, not only by denying.

lessons.title: Listen for yourself before judging
lessons.body: Most opponents have never heard the real message; Umar heard first-hand and was moved.

lessons.title: Weak reports may be used in sirah with conditions
lessons.body: A weak report is not fabricated; it can be told in sirah with rules.

lessons.title: Knowing the truth is not accepting it
lessons.body: Al-Walid admitted the Quran is not man's words but rejected it out of interest.

lessons.title: Stand as a minority
lessons.body: Under pressure to hide identity, choose 'fight' over 'flight'.

lessons.title: Sirah and Quran explain each other
lessons.body: Understanding sirah helps understand the Quran and vice versa.

A lasting feeling of inferiority, especially among minorities.
A hadith weak in its chain but not fabricated.
Physical pressure and threats to frighten.

dalil.context: Allah gave the Prophet SAW Al-Kawthar. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: We have truly given abundance to you [Prophet]––

dalil.context: The meaning of Al-Kawthar explained.
dalil.translation: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise and the Prophet's SAW pool; its width is a month's journey, its water whiter than milk and sweeter than musk, its cups like the stars, and whoever drinks will never be thirsty.

dalil.context: It is the one who hates the Prophet SAW who is cut off. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: it is the one who hates you who has been cut off.

dalil.context: The Prophet SAW lived among them all his life before the Quran; will they not reflect?
dalil.translation: Say, ‘If God had so willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I lived a whole lifetime among you before it came to me. How can you not use your reason?’

dalil.context: You are not mad, by the grace of your Lord. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Your Lord’s grace does not make you [Prophet] a madman:

dalil.context: Their hostile glances nearly make the Prophet SAW slip as they say he is mad.
dalil.translation: The disbelievers almost strike you down with their looks when they hear the Quran. They say, ‘He must be mad!’

dalil.context: They said, 'O you to whom the Reminder was sent, you are mad.'
dalil.translation: They say, ‘Receiver of this Quran! You are definitely mad.

dalil.context: They marvel at a warner from among them and call him a sorcerer and a liar.
dalil.translation: The disbelievers think it strange that a prophet of their own people has come to warn them: they say, ‘He is just a lying sorcerer.

dalil.context: The wealthy of Quraysh mocked the poor followers.
dalil.translation: We have made some of them a test for others, to make the disbelievers say, ‘Is it these men that God has favoured among us?’ Does God not know best who are the grateful ones?

dalil.context: Allah tells the Prophet SAW to stay patient with those who call on their Lord morning and evening. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Content yourself with those who pray to their Lord morning and evening, seeking His approval, and do not let your eyes turn away from them out of desire for the attractions of this worldly life: do not yield to those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our Quran, those who follow their own low desires, those whose ways are unbridled.

dalil.context: The wrongdoers laughed at the believers.
dalil.translation: The wicked used to laugh at the believers––

dalil.context: A consolation for the minority who hold on to their faith.
dalil.translation: Islam began as a stranger and will return as a stranger, so blessed are the strangers.

dalil.context: Shows the level of Umar's intelligence and strength.
dalil.translation: If Umar had lived in the time of Banu Israel he would have been a prophet.

dalil.context: The Quran is the word of a noble messenger, not the word of a poet; recited when Umar was listening.
dalil.translation: this [Quran] is the speech of an honoured messenger,

dalil.context: Nor is it the word of a soothsayer.
dalil.translation: nor the words of a soothsayer- how little you reflect!

dalil.context: Had the Prophet SAW invented sayings in Our name, We would have cut his aorta. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
